Subject: DPA clarifications: notification timeline, subprocessor notice, and evidence escrow

Vanessa —

Thanks for taking our call last week. We're reviewing the draft DPA and have a few open items we need clarified before legal signs:

1) Notification window: your draft is silent on whether the 72-hour notice is for suspected vs confirmed incidents. We need an explicit trigger so our downstream regulators can rely on a deterministic commitment.

2) Subprocessor alerts: we want an acknowledgement timeline for when Redwood informs us that a subprocessor is implicated (we usually ask vendors for 48 hours after vendor acknowledgement).

3) Evidence access: our security team needs to understand whether you will escrow telemetry/forensic snapshots or provide temporary direct access. Escrow is acceptable but we need retention and transfer guarantees.

I've attached a short RFI with the questions mapped to clauses. Can we get a short written response and a legal redline by EOD Tuesday? If redlines aren't possible, propose times for a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Jacob
Jacob Myers
Head of Vendor Risk, FinBridge

Subject: DPA - proposed redlines for incident & subprocessor clauses

Jacob/Vanessa —

Attached is a focused redline (DPA_redline_incident_clauses.docx) that targets the items you flagged. High-level summary of proposed language:

• Trigger: initial notification obligation will be to provide an "Initial Notification" within 72 hours of Redwood's confirmed determination that a security event constitutes a data incident affecting FinBridge data. We declined a 72h "suspected" trigger due to operational false positives; we do include an obligation to "notify promptly of suspected incidents" in an earlier communication channel.

• Subprocessor notice: Redwood will notify Customer of any implicated subprocessor within 48 hours of Redwood obtaining acknowledgment from that subprocessor that their services were implicated. Customer may then request subprocessor-specific evidence within 14 days.

• Evidence access vs escrow: We propose two options in the redline: (1) short-term escrow of compressed forensic snapshots (retained for 90 days) delivered to a mutually agreed escrow holder upon written request, or (2) secure ephemeral access via a time-limited tenant slice and remote read-only forensic share for up to 14 days. We note that escrow requires procurement and cost lines; ephemeral access avoids long-term custody.

• International transfers: For cross-border evidence exports, Redwood will comply with applicable law and provide redacted telemetry when necessary; where lawful transfer is not available, Redwood will assist with in‑country review sessions under NDA.

Next steps: I can incorporate FinBridge's preference (escrow vs ephemeral access) into the redline and return a consolidated DPA. Please confirm preference and any regulator-driven constraints.

Attachment: DPA_redline_incident_clauses.docx (word doc stub)

Kimberly Park
Staff Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear options. A couple quick answers from our side:

1) Trigger: We prefer 'confirmed' as the contractual trigger but require that the contract expressly states that a suspected-incident channel exists for early coordination and regulator engagement.

2) Subprocessor notice: 48 hours after subprocessor acknowledgement is acceptable. Please add language that allows FinBridge to request a dedicated subprocessor statement and a scoped log export within 14 days.

3) Evidence access: FinBridge leans toward ephemeral access over escrow if Redwood can guarantee immutable snapshots and audit logs of access. If escrow is chosen, we need an SLA for release and chain-of-custody documentation.

Attached is the RFI with a short regulator note that we can share with your legal if helpful. Let's proceed with the ephemeral access default and escrow as fallback. We can sign off once the redline includes: initial 72h confirmed notification, subprocessor 48h ack, subproc-scoped export 14d, ephemeral access details (14d window, read-only, immutable snapshot).

Happy to take the 30-min slot Tuesday at 10:30 ET.

Jacob

Date: 2027-09-14T08:00:00-04:00
Subject: Technical constraints and proposed evidence access workflow

Jacob/Kim/Vanessa —

Quick technical note from Security: the ephemeral access model is feasible and aligns with our current incident playbook. Proposed implementation sketch:

• Immutable snapshot: we take a timebound snapshot of relevant telemetry and a read-only VM image. Snapshot is write-protected and time-stamped.

• Delivery: rather than long-term escrow, we provide an S3 presigned, access-limited bundle behind a customer-specific IAM role for 14 days. All access is logged and a SHA256 manifest is included for chain of custody.

• Subprocessor exports: we can deliver scoped logs for a named subprocessor within 14 days where contractually permitted; note that third-party vendor logs sometimes require vendor consent which can add latency. We will include a clause describing reasonable-effort cooperation and an exception for vendor-nondisclosure.

• Cost/Procurement: escrow storage or third-party escrow accounts will incur an implementation fee and monthly storage charges; ephemeral access avoids those fees.

I'll prepare a short appendix for the redline that describes the technical knobs (snapshot retention, manifest/hash, access TTL).

Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
